updates.name: Cathy Whitlock
updates.bio: Regents Professor Emerita in Montana State University's Department of Earth Sciences, a Fellow of the Montana Institute on Ecosystems and past director of the MSU Paleoecology Lab. Research addresses Quaternary environmental change, reconstructing past vegetation, fire regimes and climate across the western United States and southern South America, and applying paleoecology to conservation.
updates.research_interests: Quaternary paleoecology and environmental change; vegetation, fire and climate history of the western US and southern South America; conservation uses of paleoecology; Cenozoic climate variability; comparing past-climate data with models
updates.current_title: Regents Professor Emerita; Fellow, Montana Institute on Ecosystems; Past Director, MSU Paleoecology Lab
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Earth Sciences, Montana State University
updates.evidence: Dr. Cathy Whitlock Regents Professor Emerita Fellow, Montana Institute on Ecosystems Past Director, MSU Paleoecology Lab
updates.notes: Existing homepage https://www.montana.edu/earthsciences/faculty/whitlock.html now 404; the department directory page /earthsciences/directory/cathy_whitlock.html (200) lists her as Regents Professor Emerita. Its selected contributions include Yellowstone work (2024 fecal-biomarker record from a northern Yellowstone catchment; 2020 Yellowstone Lake radiocarbon paper), consistent with the YNP-LT collaborator row. The older MSU Paleoecology Lab Google Site page still shows 'Regents Professor' and 'Lead Investigator, NSF WildFIRE PIRE'. No ORCID or Google Scholar link on either page. ORCID 0000-0002-1585-1209 (Cathy Whitlock) has no employments or URLs, so it could not be tied to MSU and was not recorded. Verifier 2026-10-26: re-fetched both pages; dropped the unsupported 'Paleoecologist' label from the bio and corrected the note that cited a 2020 fire-history paper whose listed authors do not include her.

updates.name: Paul D. Brooks
updates.bio: Professor of Geology and Geophysics at the University of Utah since July 2014, also listed with the Interdisciplinary Program in Hydrology and Water Resources. The research group studies how water, energy and nutrients cycle through catchments with seasonal snow cover, and works with stakeholders to forecast climate and land-use effects on snowpack, melt and downstream water supplies.
updates.research_interests: water, energy and biogeochemical cycling in seasonally snow-covered catchments; climate and land-use effects on snow accumulation, ablation and snowmelt-fed water resources; stakeholder-engaged prediction
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Geology & Geophysics, University of Utah
